stem.text: Consider the curve given by \( \left(y - 3\right)^{2} = \left(- x - 8\right)^{2}\left(- x - 5\right) \). Find all points on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

answer_key.label: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (-6, 5) \) and \( (-6, 1) \).

worked_solution.text: The numerator is zero where \( x = -8 \) or \( x = -6 \). At \( x = -8 \) the curve gives \( y = 3 \), where the denominator is also zero, so no horizontal tangent is decided there.
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator zero with a nonzero denominator

worked_solution.text: At \( x = -6 \) the relation gives \( \left(y - 3\right)^{2} = 4 \), so \( y = 5 \) or \( y = 1 \), and the denominator is not zero at either.
worked_solution.rule_named: solve the relation and the condition together

worked_solution.text: The tangent line is horizontal only at the points \( (-6, 5) \) and \( (-6, 1) \).
